common_name: Amazon Dwarf Mistflower (Compact Non-Spreading Blue Mistflower)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in moist to average, slightly acidic to neutral soil in partial shade to full sun in spring; Amazon Dwarf is a compact selection of native blue mistflower bred for a tidier, less aggressively spreading habit than the wild species.

directions: Plant divisions in moist to average, slightly acidic to neutral soil in partial shade to full sun. Amazon Dwarf is a compact selection of native blue mistflower, staying under 15 inches with a tighter, less rhizome-spreading habit than the wild species, making it a more manageable choice for a mixed border or small bed while retaining the same frothy, powder-blue flower clusters that open in late summer into fall. Its late-season bloom is an outstanding nectar source for migrating monarch butterflies and other pollinators at a time when few other perennials are still flowering. Unlike many fall-blooming natives, it tolerates considerable shade and works well in naturalistic plantings, rain gardens, and woodland edges throughout the Gulf South.
sources: Louisiana State University AgCenter — Louisiana Super Plants Program
